1: Load = 50 Ω = Z₀: the load takes the whole wave, nothing comes back
2: Open end (∞ Ω): no current can flow, the whole wave turns around
3: Short (0 Ω): the voltage must stay 0, the wave comes back upside down
4: Any load: at the end, voltage / current must equal Z_L. That fixes size and sign of the reflection.
5: 100 Ω: in between, part of the wave is absorbed, part comes back
6: Γ (reflection coefficient) only depends on how far Z_L is from Z₀
7: Power goes with the square: with 100 Ω, (1/3)² = 11 % of the power comes back
8: In dB: |S11| = 20 · log₁₀|Γ|. The more negative, the better the match (Return Loss).
9: That is why the SNA has a 50 → 75 Ω pad: an SDI cable directly on 50 Ω would reflect at −14 dB
10: Real loads change with frequency, e.g. 50 Ω with 2 pF of connector capacitance in parallel
11: Low frequency: the capacitor is almost open, the load is a good 50 Ω
12: Higher frequency: Z_C falls, the load drifts away from 50 Ω, more is reflected
13: Impedance over frequency = reflection over frequency. That is why the SNA sweeps.
